newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin vows to pay army debt in two-three months.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin vows to pay army debt in two-three months.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who has made military reform a top priorty for Russia, told the government on Tuesday to pay wage arrears to servicemen within two to three months, the presidential press service said.
Yeltsin met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his two first deputies, pro-market liberals Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, at an unnamed state residence on the outskirts of Moscow.
The president said other important tasks for the cabinet this year were support for domestic industries, health care and state debts to other social groups.

"The president has set a target for the government to cover in two to three months the state's debt in wages to the personnel of the armed forces of the Russian Federation," a Kremlin press statement said.
Chernomyrdin vowed on Monday to press ahead with military reform and said he had been instructed by Yeltsin to repay all debts to the army in July and August.
Chubais said on Monday the debt amounted to five trillion roubles ($864.9 million) and would be covered in three or four months. ($ = 5781 Russian Roubles)
